title: Le Blanc's own: saving faith depends somehow on will as free good work (1 Peter 1)
source_text: XVIII. Ut autem aperiam quid mihi quoque hac de re videatur, illud primo ut certum habeo, fidem veram & salvificam, ratione originis suae, a voluntate quodammodo pendere. Nec enim a quoquam in dubium vocari potest quin ejusmodi fides sit opus bonum, ac laude & praemio dignum, cui Deus salutem animae, tanquam mercedem ejus gratuitam promisit, ut docet Petrus Apostolus capite primo prioris Epistolae. Omne autem opus bonum & laudabile liberum, & voluntarium est, & a voluntate libera ortum habet.
pass_a_gloss: But that I may open what also seems to me on this matter: first I hold as certain that true and saving faith, by reason of its origin, somehow depends on the will. For it cannot be called in doubt by anyone that such faith is a good work, worthy of praise and reward, to which God has promised the soul's salvation as its gracious wages, as the Apostle Peter teaches in the first chapter of his first Epistle. But every good and praiseworthy work is free and voluntary, and has its rise from free will.
pass_b_english: Le Blanc's own first point: saving faith somehow depends on the will by origin.
It is a free good work God rewards with salvation (1 Peter 1) — hence voluntary.
